cases.name: out-of-scope-caption-dashboard
cases.promptMarkdown: I am working on HCB Desktop, an Electron app that shows live captions for hard-of-hearing users during calls. Design the caption overlay window for me: the live caption text area, the speaker labels, the pause and resume controls, and a small settings panel for font size and contrast. Also add a data dashboard view that charts caption latency and word error rate over the last hour as a table plus two charts. Give me the layout and styling approach.

Priya

……

…

Don't use italics; they're harder to read at a glance. When interim text is confirmed, only its color changes. Words never move, because text that reflows mid-sentence is the biggest readability problem in live captions. - **Font:** system sans, weight 500, `line-height: 1.35`, `letter-spacing: 0.01em`. Each speaker also gets a 4px colored bar (`.speaker-key`) on the left of their block. Color is a second cue, never the only one, so the overlay works for colorblind users and in high-contrast mode. - Assign colors by speaker identity, in join order, using fixed slots that are never cycled. Blue, orange and aqua stay distinguishable in both light and dark modes. From the fourth speaker on, the bar is a neutral gray and only the name identifies them. A speaker keeps their color for the whole call even if others leave. - Unknown speakers show as "Speaker 1", "Speaker 2", and so on, never as a blank. ### Pause / resume - **Recommended behavior:** pause freezes the display so the user can read, while capture keeps running in the background. Putting them on two y-axes invites false correlation. Instead, stack the two charts at the same width so their time axes line up, and link their crosshairs. - **Stat tiles above the charts:** latency p50, latency p95, and WER over the last hour. Each tile shows the change against the previous hour, with an icon and a sign so it isn't color alone. Leave 24px between sections and 16px padding inside cards. ### Chart specs - **Latency chart:** two series. p50 is blue (`#2a78d6` light / `#3987e5` dark) and p95 is orange (`#eb6834` / `#d95926`). Because there are two series, it gets a legend, plus labels at the end of each line. Add a 1px muted reference line at the latency target labeled "2 s target" in muted ink. Don't use a status color for the target line. - **WER chart:** one series in blue. The title names it, so it needs no legend. Start the y-axis at 0% and leave the top on auto. - **Marks:** 2px lines with round joins, an 8px end dot with a 2px ring in the surface color, and an optional 10% opacity area wash under p50 only. Gridlines are 1px solid hairlines (`#e1e0d9` light / `#2c2c2a` dark). Axis ticks use muted ink with `tabular-nums`: x-axis every 10 minutes (`14:10`), y-axis rounded (`0 / 500 / 1,000`). - **Gaps:** when a minute has no captions (silence), break the line. Don't connect across the gap or draw zero. - **Hover:** a vertical crosshair snaps to the nearest minute. The tooltip shows the time and every value at that minute, using text-colored values next to small color keys. Hovering one chart moves the crosshair on the other. Arrow keys move the crosshair once a chart has focus. - **Text never uses the series color.** Labels, values and the legend use primary, secondary or muted ink. Identity comes from the colored line or dot next to the text. - **Dark mode** uses the dark color values listed above against a `#1a1a19` surface. Set it with `data-theme` and also respect `prefers-color-scheme`. ### Table - One row per minute, newest first. Columns: Time, p50 ms, p95 ms, WER %, Words, Status. - Numbers are right-aligned with `tabular-nums`. The header is sticky. - Status shows as an icon plus a word ("✓ OK", "⚠ Slow", "✕ Degraded"), with status colors applied only to the icon. - The table is collapsed by default, with a "Copy CSV" button. ### Data plumbing The main process aggregates recognizer events into 1-minute buckets in a 60-slot ring buffer. Each bucket holds the p50 and p95 latency (from the gap between audio timestamp and render) and WER. Measuring WER needs reference transcripts, so in production you'll probably have user corrections or sampled audits rather than true WER. Label the chart honestly, e.g. "Estimated WER (from corrections)". The main process sends a snapshot over IPC once a minute and streams the current partial bucket every 5 s. For the charts, uPlot is small and fast and can redraw every second. Recharts is fine if the dashboard is in React. Either way, keep the color and size values in CSS custom properties, not inside the chart code. --- **Decisions for you:** 1. Should pause freeze the display while capture continues (my recommendation), or stop recognition? 2. Where will WER come from? If you tell me your renderer stack, I can scaffold both windows.

# 1. Caption overlay window

## Electron window setup
- A frameless, transparent `BrowserWindow` with `alwaysOnTop: true` at level `'screen-saver'` so it stays above full-screen call apps. Call `setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces(true)`.
- Default size is about 720×200. It docks to the bottom-center of the active display, can be resized by the user, and remembers its position per display.
- **Optional click-through mode:** `setIgnoreMouseEvents(true, { forward: true })`. When the pointer hovers over the control strip, turn mouse events back on so users can always get to the controls.
- Drag region: the header strip uses `-webkit-app-region: drag`. Every button inside it uses `no-drag`.

## Layout
```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ● LIVE   [⏸ Pause]                        [Aa] [⤢] [✕]    │  ← control strip, 36px, fades to 30% when idle
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ▍Maria Chen                                                │
│ ▍ so the release is moving to Thursday because              │
│ ▍Dev (You)                                                 │
│ ▍ okay that works for me, I'll update the ticket_           │  ← interim words
│                                       [↓ Jump to live]     │  ← only shown after the user scrolls up
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Caption text area
- **Line length:** text is capped at about 60ch per line, and 2 to 4 lines are visible (user setting, default 3). Older lines scroll up. Don't fade them out, because people re-read.
- **Anchored to the bottom, append-only.** Final words never reflow or jump. While the user is scrolled up, auto-scroll pauses and a "Jump to live" pill appears.
- **Interim vs. final words:** interim words keep full contrast and get a dotted underline. Don't use gray "pending" text. Users need to read it immediately, and low contrast hurts exactly the people this app is for.
- **Corrections:** when the recognizer rewrites an interim word, swap it without animation. With `prefers-reduced-motion` off, a 150 ms background flash on the changed word is enough.
- **Type:** system sans (`system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI"`), weight 500, line-height 1.4. Never use condensed or thin weights.
- **Accessibility:** the container has `role="log"`. Leave `aria-live` **off** by default, because screen-reader users on a call don't want every word spoken. Expose it as a setting.

## Speaker labels
- The speaker's name appears on its own line above their turn, in bold at 0.8× the caption size and in secondary ink. Label your own speech "(You)".
- **Identity is never color alone.** Each speaker gets a 4px left bar in a stable color, but the name text always carries the identity. Colors follow the speaker, not join order: once Maria is blue she stays blue all call. Use categorical slots 1 to 3 (blue `#3987e5`, orange `#d95926`, aqua `#199e70` on dark). Past 3 speakers, the bar turns neutral and the name does the work.
- Caption text always uses the ink color, never the speaker color.
- For an unknown speaker, show "Speaker 2". Clicking the label lets the user rename them for the session.

## Pause / resume
Decide what pause means, because there are two different actions, and make that choice visible in the UI:
- **Pause captions** stops audio capture and recognition, which matters for privacy. The control strip shows a large toggle button with icon and label (`⏸ Pause` / `▶ Resume`). Never use an icon-only button here.
- When paused, the caption area shows a persistent banner: "⏸ Captions paused — nothing is being transcribed". It uses an icon and text, not just a color change. The LIVE dot becomes a hollow ring labeled "PAUSED".
- Add a global shortcut through `globalShortcut` (e.g. ⌘/Ctrl+Shift+K) that works while the call app has focus, and show it in the button's tooltip.
- On resume, insert a hairline divider with the time gap ("— resumed 14:32 —") so the user knows they missed something.

## Settings panel (popover from the [Aa] button)
A 280px popover anchored inside the overlay. Changes apply live with no Save button. Persist them with `electron-store`.

| Control | Type | Values |
|---|---|---|
| Font size | Segmented control + preview | S 20 / M 26 / L 32 / XL 40 px |
| Contrast | Swatch buttons, each rendering "Aa" in its own colors | White on black · Black on white · Yellow on black · Follow system (forced-colors) |
| Background opacity | Slider | 60–100%, default 85% |
| Visible lines | Stepper | 2–4 |
| Speaker colors | Toggle | On by default |

Make every option at least 32px tall, keyboard reachable, and close the popover with Esc.

## Styling approach

# HCB Desktop: caption overlay and dashboard design

The repo is empty, so this is a design spec with starter code, not wired-in files. Two principles apply to both screens:

- **Captions come first.** Controls never cover the text, and nothing moves unless it has to.
- **Color never carries meaning by itself.** Speaker names, status and chart series always have a text label too.

---

## 1. Caption overlay window

### Electron window

```js
const overlay = new BrowserWindow({
  width: 900, height: 220, minWidth: 480, minHeight: 140,
  frame: false, transparent: true, resizable: true,
  alwaysOnTop: true, skipTaskbar: true, hasShadow: false,
  webPreferences: { preload, contextIsolation: true, sandbox: true },
});
overlay.setAlwaysOnTop(true, 'screen-saver');     // stays above fullscreen call windows
overlay.setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces(true, { visibleOnFullScreen: true });
```

- **Click-through:** turn on `setIgnoreMouseEvents(true, { forward: true })` when the pointer is over the caption text. Turn it off when the pointer enters the control strip, so the call window underneath stays usable.
- **Global shortcuts:** `globalShortcut` for pause/resume (`⌥⇧Space`), bigger/smaller text (`⌥⇧=`/`⌥⇧-`), and show/hide (`⌥⇧C`). Users shouldn't have to find a small button during a call.
- **Saved state:** store window position, size, font size and contrast preset with `electron-store`.

### Layout

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ● LIVE   Paused · 12 new lines ↓          [⏸] [Aa] [⋯]  ⠿    │ ← control strip (32px, fades to 0.4 when idle)
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ▌Priya    So the rollout is moving to Thursday because       │
│           the vendor needs one more day.                     │
│ ▌Marcus   Okay — does that affect the training session?      │
│ ▌Priya    It shouldn't, we'll keep it on Fri|                │ ← in-progress line
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

```css
.overlay { display: grid; grid-template-rows: auto 1fr; height: 100vh;
  background: var(--cap-bg); border-radius: 12px; overflow: hidden; }
.captions { overflow-y: auto; padding: 12px 20px 16px;
  font: 500 var(--cap-size)/1.4 system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif;
  color: var(--cap-ink); scroll-behavior: auto; }
.turn { display: grid; grid-template-columns: max-content 1fr; column-gap: 14px;
  margin-block-end: 0.35em; }
.speaker { font-size: 0.7em; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: .02em;
  color: var(--cap-ink-2); padding-inline-start: 10px;
  border-inline-start: 4px solid var(--speaker-color); align-self: baseline; }
.text.interim { color: var(--cap-ink-2); }          /* in-progress words: dimmer, never below 4.5:1 */
.text.interim::after { content: "▍"; animation: blink 1s steps(1) infinite; }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .text.interim::after { animation: none; } }
```

**Caption text area**
- Show 2 to 4 visible lines by default. Hold each line still and only append to it; don't reflow text that's already shown. Text that jumps around is the biggest readability problem in live captions.
- Show in-progress (interim) words in the secondary ink color. When they become final, switch them to primary in place without animating. Don't use italic, which is harder to read at size.
- Auto-scroll keeps the newest line at the bottom, but only while the user is at the bottom. If they scroll up, it pauses automatically (same as the pause button).
- For accessibility, use `role="log"` with `aria-live="off"` by default. Spoken announcements would compete with the call audio. Offer an opt-in setting that switches it to `polite` and only announces finished sentences.

**Speaker labels**
- The speaker's name is always printed as text. The colored bar on the left is an extra cue.
- Each speaker gets a color from a fixed palette, in order of first appearance, and keeps it for the whole session. If a speaker leaves, nobody else gets recolored.
- After 6 speakers, the rest share a neutral gray bar and are told apart by name only.
- Group consecutive lines from the same speaker under one label. Show the label again only when the speaker changes.

**Pause / resume**
- Pausing freezes the display, but transcription keeps buffering underneath. The status chip changes from `● LIVE` to `Paused · N new lines ↓`.
- Resuming, or clicking the chip, jumps to the live position.
- The button changes its icon and its `aria-label` together ("Pause captions" / "Resume captions") and uses `aria-pressed`.
- The status shows a word and an icon, not just a red or green dot.

**Settings popover (`Aa`)**

It sits on top of the window, anchored to the button, so the caption area never shrinks. It has three groups:

| Control | Type | Values |
|---|---|---|
| Text size | Slider + −/+ buttons with a live preview line | 18–64px, default 28px, steps of 2 |
| Contrast | Radio swatches, each labeled | White on black · Black on white · Yellow on black · Black on yellow · System |
| Background opacity | Slider | 60–100% (contrast is checked against the worst case) |

```css
.overlay[data-contrast="white-on-black"]  { --cap-bg: rgb(0 0 0 / var(--bg-a)); --cap-ink: #fff;    --cap-ink-2: #c8c8c8; }
.overlay[data-contrast="black-on-white"]  { --cap-bg: rgb(255 255 255 / var(--bg-a)); --cap-ink: #000; --cap-ink-2: #444; }
.overlay[data-contrast="yellow-on-black"] { --cap-bg: rgb(0 0 0 / var(--bg-a)); --cap-ink: #ffeb3b; --cap-ink-2: #d9c84a; }
.overlay[data-contrast="black-on-yellow"] { --cap-bg: rgb(255 235 59 / var(--bg-a)); --cap-ink: #000; --cap-ink-2: #3a3500; }
@media (forced-colors: active) {
  .overlay { background: Canvas; color: CanvasText; }
  .speaker { border-color: CanvasText; }
}
```

- The background opacity floor is 60%. Below that, the contrast depends on whatever is underneath, so it can't be guaranteed.
- Close the popover with `Esc`. Every control is reachable by keyboard and has a visible 2px focus ring.

---

## 2. Data dashboard: latency and word error rate (WER), last hour

This opens as a separate normal window (not always-on-top) from the `⋯` menu.

### Form choices

- **Two separate charts, one above the other, sharing the time axis.** Don't use one chart with two y-axes: latency in milliseconds and WER in percent have different scales, and a dual-axis chart suggests correlations that aren't real.
- **Latency chart:** p50 as a 2px line, with a lighter p95 band behind it. Add a dashed target line labeled "Target 1.5 s" (the number is a placeholder; use your own target).
- **WER chart:** a 2px line per minute, with the y-axis starting at 0%. Add a dashed threshold line, e.g. "10%".
- **No legends.** Each chart has one series and its title names it. The p95 band gets a small direct label at the right edge.
- Above the charts, a row of **stat tiles**: Current p50 latency · p95 latency (1 h) · Avg WER (1 h) · Minutes over target. When a value is over target, show a status color plus an icon and text ("⚠ Over target"), never color alone.

### Layout

```
┌ Caption quality ─────────────── [Last hour ▾] [All speakers ▾] [⟳ Live] ┐
│ ┌p50 latency┐ ┌p95 latency┐ ┌Avg WER┐ ┌Over target┐                    │
│ │  820 ms   │ │  1.9 s ⚠  │ │ 7.4 % │ │ 4 min     │                    │
│ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────┘ └───────────┘                    │
│ Caption latency (ms)                                                    │
│ ▁▂▃▂▂▃▅▃▂ ─ ─ ─ Target 1.5 s ─ ─ ─                    [chart 220px]      │
│ Word error rate (%)                                                     │
│ ▂▂▁▂▃▂▂▂▂ ─ ─ ─ 10% ─ ─ ─                              [chart 220px]      │
│ ──────────────────────────────────────────────── 14:00 … 15:00          │
│ Per-minute data                                  [Download CSV]         │
│ Time  │ p50 ms │ p95 ms │ WER % │ Words │ Status                        │
│ 14:59 │   790  │  1,420 │  6.8  │  142  │ ✓ OK                          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

```css
.dash { display: grid; gap: 16px; padding: 24px; max-width: 1200px; margin-inline: auto;
  grid-template-areas: "filters" "tiles" "latency" "wer" "table"; background: var(--page); }
.tiles { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(180px, 1fr)); gap: 12px; }
.chart-card { background: var(--surface-1); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 10px; padding: 16px; }
.chart-card h2 { font: 600 14px/1.3 system-ui; color: var(--text-primary); margin: 0 0 8px; }
.table-wrap { max-height: 360px; overflow: auto; }
table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font: 13px system-ui; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
thead th { position: sticky; top: 0; background: var(--surface-1); text-align: end; color: var(--text-secondary); }
td { text-align: end; padding: 6px 10px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--grid); }
td:first-child, th:first-child { text-align: start; }
```

### Chart styling

- Both lines use one series color, blue `--series-1` (`#2a78d6` light / `#3987e5` dark). The p95 band is the same blue at about 18% opacity.
- Gridlines are faint hairlines (`#e1e0d9` light / `#2c2c2a` dark). Axis labels are muted gray `#898781` with tabular figures. Show at most 4 to 5 y-axis ticks, and an x-axis label every 10 minutes.
- Labels, values and tooltips always use the normal text colors, never the blue.
- **Hover:** a vertical crosshair and tooltip that are synced across both charts. Hovering 14:32 on one shows 14:32 on the other, e.g. "14:32 · p50 810 ms · p95 1.6 s". The hit area is the whole column, not just the 2px line.
- **Keyboard:** each chart is focusable, and ←/→ steps the crosshair one minute at a time.
- **Live updates:** append one point per minute with no animated redraw. A `⟳ Live` toggle freezes the view while someone is inspecting it.
- **Dark mode:** use the dark color tokens from the reference palette, chosen per mode rather than auto-inverted, and follow both the OS setting and an in-app theme toggle.
- **The table** is also the accessible view of the charts. It has 60 rows, newest first, a sticky header, the same Status icon and text as the tiles, and a CSV export.

### Implementation notes

- **Charts:** a light SVG chart library (uPlot or Recharts), or plain D3. uPlot handles 60-point live updates very cheaply and has built-in cursor sync between charts.
- **Data:** the main process aggregates per-minute buckets and pushes them over IPC (`caption-metrics:update`). The renderer keeps a 60-entry ring buffer.
- **How latency is measured:** from the end of the audio chunk to the final caption appearing on screen. Show interim-caption latency separately if you track it. Mixing the two would make latency look worse than users actually experience.
- **WER needs reference transcripts:** live calls don't have them. Compute WER from sampled corrections, or from a "Quality mode" that runs a second, stronger transcription pass. The dashboard subtitle should say which source it uses.

### Still to check

- **Speaker colors:** I haven't run the color-contrast checker against the overlay's own backgrounds, because I had no shell in this session. Before shipping, run `validate_palette.js` with `--surface #000000 --mode dark` and with the yellow background. Use only the colors that pass on all four contrast presets; otherwise fall back to neutral bars and names only.
- **Example values:** the latency target (1.5 s) and the WER threshold (10%) are placeholders. Set them to your real product targets.

I can scaffold this as real files next: the overlay window, a preload bridge, the React overlay and settings components, and the dashboard with uPlot.

.overlay { display: grid; grid-template-rows: auto 1fr; height: 100vh;

.captions { overflow-y: auto; padding: 12px 20px 16px;

.turn { display: grid; grid-template-columns: max-content 1fr; column-gap: 14px;

.text.interim { color: var(--cap-ink-2); }          /* in-progress words: dimmer, never below 4.5:1 */

**Caption text area**
- Show 2 to 4 visible lines by default. Hold each line still and only append to it; don't reflow text that's already shown. Text that jumps around is the biggest readability problem in live captions.
- Show in-progress (interim) words in the secondary ink color. When they become final, switch them to primary in place without animating. Don't use italic, which is harder to read at size.
- Auto-scroll keeps the newest line at the bottom, but only while the user is at the bottom. If they scroll up, it pauses automatically (same as the pause button).
- For accessibility, use `role="log"` with `aria-live="off"` by default. Spoken announcements would compete with the call audio. Offer an opt-in setting that switches it to `polite` and only announces finished sentences.

**Speaker labels**
- The speaker's name is always printed as text. The colored bar on the left is an extra cue.
- Each speaker gets a color from a fixed palette, in order of first appearance, and keeps it for the whole session. If a speaker leaves, nobody else gets recolored.
- After 6 speakers, the rest share a neutral gray bar and are told apart by name only.
- Group consecutive lines from the same speaker under one label. Show the label again only when the speaker changes.

- Pausing freezes the display, but transcription keeps buffering underneath. The status chip changes from `● LIVE` to `Paused · N new lines ↓`.
- Resuming, or clicking the chip, jumps to the live position.
- The button changes its icon and its `aria-label` together ("Pause captions" / "Resume captions") and uses `aria-pressed`.

**Settings popover (`Aa`)**

| Control | Type | Values |
|---|---|---|
| Text size | Slider + −/+ buttons with a live preview line | 18–64px, default 28px, steps of 2 |

It follows the system light/dark theme, with a manual override. ## Layout ``` ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Caption quality [Last 15 min | 30 min | 1 hour ✓] ⟳ live │ ← one filter row, scopes everything ├──────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Caption latency │ Word error rate │ │ p50 and p95, seconds │ % of words, per minute │ │ ── p95 2.1│ 6.8% │ │ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ target 1.5 s ─ ─ ─│ │ │ ── p50 0.9│ │ │ 14:05 14:20 14:35 14:50 │ 14:05 14:20 14:35 14:50 │ ├──────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Per-minute detail │ │ Time p50 latency p95 latency WER Words Status │ │ 15:04 0.9 s 2.1 s 6.8% 142 ⚠ Above target │ │ 15:03 0.8 s 1.4 s 5.2% 131 ✓ OK │ │ … │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` CSS grid: `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(360px, 1fr))` for the chart row, with the table spanning the full width. Below about 760px the charts stack vertically. ## Chart decisions - **Two charts, never one dual-axis chart.** Latency (seconds) and WER (%) have unrelated scales. Putting them on one plot with two y-axes invites false correlations. - **Latency chart:** line chart with 60 one-minute buckets and two series, p50 (series slot 1, blue) and p95 (slot 2, orange). It has a legend, and each line is labeled at its right end ("p95 2.1 s"). The target (e.g. 1.5 s) is a hairline reference line in muted ink, with a text label. The lines are never recolored when they cross it. - **WER chart:** a single line in slot 1 blue with a ~10% area wash. No legend is needed because the title names the series. The y-axis starts at 0% so small changes don't look dramatic. The latest value is labeled at the line's end. - **Mark specs:** - Lines: 2px with round joins. - End-dots: at least 8px, with a 2px ring in the surface color. - Gridlines: 1px solid hairlines (`#e1e0d9` light / `#2c2c2a` dark), horizontal only. - Axis text: muted `#898781`, `tabular-nums`, clean ticks (0 / 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 s). - **Gaps are not zeros.** Minutes with no speech break the line. Don't draw them as 0, because that would look like perfect latency. - **Hover:** a vertical crosshair snaps to the nearest minute. One tooltip per chart lists every series at that minute, with the value in strong ink first and the series name after, keyed by a short line stroke. The same readout appears on keyboard focus (arrow keys step through minutes). Insert labels with `textContent`. - **Live refresh:** append a new bucket each minute. While refetching, keep the previous render at reduced opacity. No skeleton loaders and no layout jumps. ## Table - Newest row first, numbers right-aligned with `tabular-nums`, sticky header, units in the header or cells. - The Status column uses the reserved status colors **always with an icon and a word** (✓ OK / ⚠ Above target / ✕ Critical), never color alone. These colors are separate from the series colors. - The table is the accessible version of both charts. Every value in a tooltip is also in the table. It's tiny, renders 60–3,600 points instantly, and makes crosshair and tooltip hooks easy. If you're already on React, Recharts or Visx also work. Either way, apply the tokens above rather than the library's default theme. --- ## Data plumbing (brief) - The main process owns the ASR session. It streams `{speakerId, text, isFinal, tStart, tEmitted}` to the overlay over IPC. - Latency per finalized segment is `tEmitted − tSpokenEnd`. - WER needs a reference transcript. Live, you can only estimate it, e.g. from ASR confidence or periodic spot-checks against corrected text. Label the chart **"Estimated WER"** unless you have real reference text. - Keep a 60-minute ring buffer of one-minute aggregates (p50, p95, WER, word count) in the main process. The dashboard subscribes to it. If you tell me your renderer stack (React, Svelte, plain), I can scaffold the overlay window, the settings store and the dashboard as working code.

graders.name: house-rules
graders.evidence:
I used the design-taste skill to plan this. No files were written, and nothing has been rendered or checked in a browser.

**1. Design read**
A plain portfolio for a calm, exact designer. Each project gets a flat field of Stockholm façade colour with its key number set huge, and that number does the job a project image would.

**2. Idea sentence**
On this page, **the one number each of Mara's products shows its user (a balance, a dose time, a pulse)**, set on **the ochre, Falu red and harbour-green façades of Gamla stan**, becomes **the project cover**. It's typographic and needs no screenshots. Each cover has a phone-frame slot where a real screen can go later.

The interactive element is a live Stockholm clock in the contact section. It reads "It's 14:20 in Stockholm. Mara's at her desk." During office hours and "after hours, she'll reply tomorrow" outside them. Without JavaScript it shows the plain email address.

**3. Sections**
- **Nav:** a plain bar with the "Mara Lindqvist" wordmark, three links (Work, About, Contact) and one button, "Email Mara".
- **Hero:** a left-aligned headline at about 9vw with one sentence under it. The lower half of the screen is a row of six tall coloured strips, one per project, like a row of house fronts on Västerlånggatan. Each strip shows its key number and links to that project.
- **Work, first two projects:** each fills the full width in its own colour. The number sits huge on one side, and the name, client, year and one-liner sit on the other, with sides alternating.
- **Work, middle two projects:** these two sit side by side as halves, each with the number on top and the text below, to change the rhythm.
- **Work, last two projects:** full width again. The phone-frame slot (9:19.5) moves in front of the number, ready for a real screenshot.
- **About:** the page turns to dark ink. A short paragraph at about 32px sits on the left, with plain facts at body size on the right: eight years, fintech and health, Stockholm, how she works.
- **Contact and footer:** back to the light ground. `mara@lindqvist.studio` is set at display size as the link, the Stockholm clock sits under it, and her name runs full width as the close.

**Sample projects (all invented, for you to replace):**

| Project | Client | Year | Number on cover | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kvitto | Norrbank | 2025 | −312 kr | Shared expenses reduced to one figure per friend. |
| Dosa | Vårdkollen | 2024 | 08:00 | A medication reminder that older patients actually keep using. |
| Spara | Lagom Bank | 2023 | 62 % | Savings goals for people opening their first account. |
| Remiss | Kliniken Söder | 2023 | Day 14 | Patients can follow a referral instead of phoning to ask about it. |
| Faktura | Moln Pay | 2022 | 3 days | Invoicing for freelancers, from sent to paid. |
| Puls | Hjärtverket | 2021 | 72 bpm | A home cardiac rehab programme people finish. |

**4. First screen**
- Headline: **Calm screens for money and health** (33 characters, so it fits on two lines)
- Supporting sentence: *I'm Mara Lindqvist, a product designer in Stockholm who has spent eight years making banking and care apps that people understand at a glance.*
- Button: **Email Mara**, which opens a `mailto:` link with a subject already filled in.

**5. Tokens**
```css
:root {
  /* colour roles */
  --ground:      #F1F2EF; /* winter-light grey, not cream */
  --ground-step: #E6E8E4; /* surface tone step, replaces lines */
  --ink:         #14181F; /* running text, full strength */
  --ink-soft:    #4A515C; /* secondary notes only */
  --accent:      #A3372A; /* Falu red: the email button and the email link only */
  --on-dark:     #F1F2EF;

  /* façade fields, one per project */
  --field-ochre:   #D6A23F; /* Kvitto */
  --field-falu:    #8E2F24; /* Dosa */
  --field-harbour: #2F4B5A; /* Spara */
  --field-moss:    #6E7F5E; /* Remiss */
  --field-plaster: #E3C9BC; /* Faktura */
  --field-slate:   #3B3F45; /* Puls */

  /* type roles: one family, Schibsted Grotesk */
  --font: "Schibsted Grotesk", system-ui, sans-serif;
  --size-display:   clamp(3.25rem, 9vw, 9.5rem);  /* headline, cover numbers */
  --size-statement: clamp(1.5rem, 2.4vw, 2.25rem); /* about paragraph, contact email */
  --size-text:      1.125rem;                      /* body, 18px */
  --size-small:     1rem;                          /* client · year */
  --track-display:  -0.04em;
  --lead-display:   0.92;
  --lead-text:      1.5;
  --weight-display: 600;
  --weight-text:    400;
  --figures:        tabular-nums;
  --measure:        62ch;

  /* space */
  --margin:  clamp(16px, 2.2vw, 32px);
  --section: clamp(96px, 13vw, 200px);
}
```

All project names, clients, years and numbers are samples to replace. Real screenshots can go into the phone-frame slots later without changing the layout. If you also want photos, Stockholm's open archives have old façade photos that could go in the About section, credited in the footer.
